## Data 

# Import

First we automatically import the data for 23 seasons of English football from the top 4 divisions.
We are pulling all our data from Football-Data.co.uk, a site containing results, match statistics and betting odds since the 2003/2004 season, and basic stats since the second Premier League season in 1993/94.

```{r}

if(!dir.exists(file.path("..", "data"))){
  dir.create(file.path("..", "data"))
}

years<-2003:2025

# Splitting up the leagues

leagues<-c(
  E0 = "Premier_League",
  E1 = "Championship",
  E2 = "League_1",
  E3 = "League_2"
)

for(year in years){
  season<-paste0(
    substr(year, 3, 4),
    sprintf("%02d", (year+1) %% 100)
  )
  
  for(league_code in names(leagues)){
    league_name<-leagues[[league_code]]
    
    
    file_name<-paste0(league_name, "_data_", season, ".csv")
    file_path<-file.path("..", "data", file_name)
    
# Only downloading if not already there
    
    if(!file.exists(file_path)){
      url<-paste0("https://football-data.co.uk/mmz4281/", season, "/", league_code, ".csv")
      message("Downloading", file_name)
      download.file(url, file_path)
    }
    else{
      message("Already exists, skipping", file_name)
    }
  }

}
```

Next creating a compiled data frame: all 4 leagues across all 23 seasons.

```{r}
files<-list.files(
  file.path("..", "data"),
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

data_list<-list()

for(i in seq_along(files)){
  df<-read.csv(files[i])
  
# This deals with a bug in the data. Some rows of certain seasons had empty strings,
# which caused additional matches to be added with no information.
  df<-df[!is.na(df$Date) & df$Date!="", ]
  
  file_name<-basename(files[i])
  
# This creates a Season variable, by recording it from the file name
  df$Season<-substr(
    file_name,
    nchar(file_name)-7,
    nchar(file_name)-4
  )
  
# Likewise this creates a League variable
  if(grepl("Premier_League", file_name)){
    df$League<-"Premier League"
  }
  else if(grepl("Championship", file_name)){
    df$League<-"Championship"
  }
  else if(grepl("League_1", file_name)){
    df$League<-"League 1"
  }
  else if(grepl("League_2", file_name)){
    df$League<-"League 2"
  }
  
  data_list[[i]]<-df
}

# This ensures that the dimensions of all the data are the same by creating N/A columns for variables
# that aren't recorded in certain seasons 
all_columns<-unique(unlist(lapply(data_list, names)))
data_list<-lapply(data_list, function(df){
  missing_columns<-setdiff(all_columns, names(df))
  df[missing_columns]<-NA
  df<-df[all_columns]
  return(df)
})

# Creating the data frame
data<-do.call(rbind, data_list)
```

```{r}
# Export to send for use in Python

write.csv(
  data,
  "../processed-data/football_data_halfclean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

We will create some important visualistation of the data to get a broader picture of it.
Firstly, a table showing how the outcomes H (Home Win), D (Draw), and A (Away Win) are distributed for each 
league over the 23 seasons:

```{r}
results_proportions<-prop.table(table(data$FTR, data$League), margin = 2)
```

```{r}
results_proportions
```

```{r}
barplot(
  results_proportions[c("H","D","A"), ],
  beside = FALSE,
  col=c("darkblue", "grey", "darkred"),
  ylim=c(0,1),
  main="Match Outcome Proportions by League",
  xlab = "League",
  ylab="Proporion of Matches"
)
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Home Win", "Draw", "Away Win"),
       fill=c("darkblue", "grey", "darkred"),
       cex=0.8)

```

Instinctively, it makes sense to remove the closing odds as variables as they are technically created with knowledge of the match outcome. We can also show how closely they interact with the opening odds for each betting site:

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(2,2))

plot(data$B365H, data$B365CH, xlab = "Bet365 Home Opening Odds", ylab = "Bet365 Home Closing Odds", main = (paste("r=", round(cor(data$B365H, data$B365CH, use = "complete.obs"), 3))))
plot(data$B365A, data$B365CA, xlab = "Bet365 Away Opening Odds", ylab = "Bet365 Away Closing Odds", main = (paste("r=", round(cor(data$B365A, data$B365CA, use = "complete.obs"), 3))))
plot(data$B365D, data$B365CD, xlab = "Bet365 Draw Opening Odds", ylab = "Bet365 Draw Closing Odds", main = (paste("r=", round(cor(data$B365D, data$B365CD, use = "complete.obs"), 3))))


par(mfrow=c(1,1))
```

We won't plot the rest of the graphs, but for the bookmakers with opening and closing odds, their correlation is shown in the below table (with N the number of observations this pulls from).

```{r}
bookmakers<-c("B365", "BW", "IW", "WH", "VC", "PS", "BF", "BFD", "BFE", "BMGM", "BV", "CL", "LB", "X1XB")
outcomes<-c("H", "D", "A")
results<-data.frame()
for (company in bookmakers){
    for (outcome in outcomes){
        opening<-paste0(company, outcome)
        closing<-paste0(company, "C", outcome)
        valid<-complete.cases(data[, c(opening, closing)])
        results<-rbind(results, data.frame(
            Bookmaker=company,
            Outcome = outcome,
            Correlation = round(cor(data[[opening]][valid], data[[closing]][valid]), 3), N=sum(valid)
        ))
    }
}

bookmakers_AH<-c("B365", "P", "BFE")
outcomes_AH<-c("H", "A")
results_AH<-data.frame()
for (company in bookmakers_AH){
    for (outcomeAH in outcomes_AH){
        opening<-paste0(company, "AH", outcome)
        closing<-paste0(company, "CAH", outcome)
        valid<-complete.cases(data[, c(opening, closing)])
        results_AH<-rbind(results_AH, data.frame(
            Bookmaker=company,
            Outcome = outcomeAH,
            Correlation = round(cor(data[[opening]][valid], data[[closing]][valid]), 3), N=sum(valid)
        ))
    }
}


bookmakers_25O<-c("B365", "BFE")
results_25O<-data.frame()
for (company in bookmakers_25O){
  opening<-paste0(company, ".2.5")
  closing<-paste0(company, "C.2.5")
  valid<-complete.cases(data[, c(opening, closing)])
  results_25O<-rbind(results_25O, data.frame(
    Bookmaker=company,
    Outcome = "Over 2.5",
    Correlation = round(cor(data[[opening]][valid], data[[closing]][valid]), 3), N=sum(valid)
  ))
}


bookmakers_25U<-c("B365", "BFE")
results_25U<-data.frame()
for (company in bookmakers_25U){
  opening<-paste0(company, ".2.5.1")
  closing<-paste0(company, "C.2.5.1")
  valid<-complete.cases(data[, c(opening, closing)])
  results_25U<-rbind(results_25U, data.frame(
    Bookmaker=company,
    Outcome = "Under 2.5",
    Correlation = round(cor(data[[opening]][valid], data[[closing]][valid]), 3), N=sum(valid)
    ))
}

results$Market<-"1X2"
results_AH$Market<-"Asian Handicap"
results_25O$Market<-"Over/Under 2.5"
results_25U$Market<-"Over/Under 2.5"
all_results<-rbind(results, results_AH, results_25O, results_25U)
all_results<-all_results[, c("Market", "Bookmaker", "Outcome", "Correlation", "N")]
all_results
```

```{r}
goal_averages<-aggregate(cbind(FTHG, FTAG) ~ League,
                         data = data,
                         FUN=mean,
                         na.rm=TRUE)
names(goal_averages)<-c("League", "Average Home Goals", "Average Away Goals")
goal_averages$`Average H-A Goal Difference`<-goal_averages$`Average Home Goals` - goal_averages$`Average Away Goals`
```

```{r}
seasons<-sort(unique(data$Season))
season_years<-2003:(2003 + length(seasons) - 1)
leagues<-unique(data$League)

par(mfrow=c(2,2))

for(league in leagues){
  league_data<-data[data$League==league, ]
  proportions<-sapply(seasons, function(s){
    matches<-league_data[league_data$Season==s, "FTR"]
    prop.table(table(factor(matches, levels = c("H", "D", "A"))))
  })
  matplot(season_years, t(proportions),
        type="l", lty = 1, lwd=2,
        col=c("blue", "green", "red"),
        ylim=c(0,1),
        main = league,
        xlab="Season", ylab = "Proportion of Matches")
  legend("right", legend = c("Home Win", "Draw", "Away Win"),
       col = c("blue", "green", "red"),
       lty=1, lwd=2, cex=0.7)
}
```



```{r}
remove_vars_0<-c(
  "Div", "Date", "HomeTeam", "AwayTeam", "Referee", "Time", "Date", "X", "Season", "League",
  "FTHG", "FTAG", "HTAG", "HTHG", "HTR"
)

closing_odds<-grep("C(H|D|A)$|C\\.|CAH|AHCh", names(data), value=TRUE)
max_avg_odds<-grep("^(Max|Avg|BbMx|BbAv)", names(data), value=TRUE)
bookmaker_counts<-grep("^Bb(1X2|OU|AH)$", names(data), value=TRUE)
odds_to_remove<-unique(c(closing_odds, max_avg_odds, bookmaker_counts))

remove_vars_1<-unique(c(remove_vars_0, odds_to_remove))

```


```{r}
remove_vars_1
```

```{r}
train_data<-data[
  data$League %in% c("Championship", "League 1", "League 2"), 
  !names(data) %in% remove_vars_1,
  drop = FALSE
]

test_data<-data[
  data$League %in% c("Premier League"), 
  !names(data) %in% remove_vars_1,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

```{r}
make_heatmap<-function(dataset, plot_title){
  numeric_data<-dataset[, sapply(dataset, is.numeric), drop = FALSE]
  usable<-sapply(numeric_data, function(x){
    sum(!is.na(x))>=2 && length(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))>1
  })
  numeric_data<-numeric_data[, usable, drop = FALSE]
  correlations<-cor(numeric_data, use="pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  heatmap_colours<-colorRampPalette(c("yellow", "orange", "red"))(100)
  heatmap(correlations, symm=TRUE, scale="none", col=heatmap_colours,
          breaks=seq(-1,1,length.out=101), main=plot_title)
  legend("topright", legend=c("Negative (~ -1)", "Zero (~ 0)", "Positive (~ +1)"),
         fill=c("yellow", "orange", "red"), cex=0.7, bty="n")
}
# Just note that the color scale should be continuous but it's hard to see, i.e. orange doesn't mean exactly 0 etc.
```

```{r}
make_heatmap(train_data, "Training Data Predictor Heatmap")
```

```{r}
make_heatmap(test_data, "Test Data Predictor Heatmap")
```
